title: The Edible Woman

vibeProfile.oneLine: A bride-to-be finds she can no longer eat, and her body speaks for her.

summary: As her wedding approaches, a young woman named Marian finds she can no longer eat, her body rebelling against a life of being consumed, packaged and defined by others. Atwood's sharp, funny first novel turns that strange symptom into a comic, unsettling fable about gender, appetite and the pressures of conventional femininity in 1960s consumer society. An early, prescient work from a writer who would spend a career dissecting the same anxieties, it is playful on the surface and pointed underneath.
whyReadIt: Atwood's sly, funny debut about a woman who literally can't stomach her own wedding. Prescient and pointed beneath the comedy.

funFacts.text: It was Atwood's first novel, written in the mid-1960s before second-wave feminism peaked.
